messages:
lia: Heads-up — seeing a ~2.4x p99 tail on the continuous batcher around 11:05-11:12 UTC. Not a full outage, but request latencies spike and then recover in a few minutes. :eyes:

sanjay: which model/shape/region? any kernel switch logs?

lia: region=us-west-2, model=orca-mini-ish (short prompts). Observed repeated kernel-selection churn on a subset of GPUs. Kernel selector flip logs show quick toggles between `fused_attn_v2` and `baseline_gemm` for the same sequence length. Also seeing frequent kvcache eviction churn. Paste from node logs:```
[11:06:12] kernel_selector: selected fused_attn_v2 (seq=128)
[11:06:12] kernel_selector: fallback -> baseline_gemm (oom_margin=12)
[11:06:13] kv_cache: evict shard=7 entries=124 usage=96%
[11:06:13] admission: microbatch created size=2 wait_ms=18
[11:06:13] admission: microbatch created size=1 wait_ms=27
[11:06:14] kernel_selector: selected fused_attn_v2 (seq=128)
[11:06:14] kernel_selector: fallback -> baseline_gemm (oom_margin=13)
```

maya: Hmm. That pattern smells like tiny requests piling up (microbatches of 1-2) while the kvcache oscillates, forcing kernel variability. Could be a noisy tenant reusing prefixes + high eviction, so KV misses + kernel memory pressure -> fallback.

devon: Agreed. I also see the batcher 'fill' metric (threadsqueeze) spike at the same time: lot of inflight small microbatches that can't coalesce because admission keeps dispatching early due to per-core queue limits. Noisy-tenant hypothesis: tenant t-42 had a sudden flood of short-lived requests at 11:04.

perf-bot: Alert: continuous-batcher tail p99=860ms (baseline ~340ms) for window 11:04-11:12. Link: https://perf.redwood/snapshot/1718601200

lia: Quick mitigation attempted: bumped `batcher.max_wait_ms` from 30 -> 60 and lowered `admission.max_queued_per_core` by 50%. Applied to us-west-2 pool via `runtimectl apply --pool us-west-2 --set batcher.max_wait_ms=60 admission.max_queued_per_core=16`

lia: After tweak, p99 dropped to ~380ms within 90s. Kernel switches stabilized and evictions reduced. Still want root-cause. :thumbsup:

maya: Nice. Can we correlate tenant t-42 traffic with KV prefix churn? If t-42 has very low prefix reuse but high QPS, it could thrash the kvcache and force frequent kernel fallback due to memory headroom changes.

sanjay: I'll pull sampled heap+nvml traces and per-tenant prefix reuse metrics. Also enabling kernel-selector debug for the affected nodes for 30m window.

devon: Suggest follow-ups: 1) instrument per-core microbatch queue lengths (new metric: queue_len_histogram), 2) record kernel-switch counts per-seq-length, 3) add an admission heuristic: prefer batching small concurrent requests from the same tenant to increase locality.

ops-oncall: Filing follow-up ticket RW-1528: "Investigate orbiting microbatches & thread-squeeze leading to kernel churn" with steps from devon. Assigning to eng-runtime + perf. I'll include the chosen mitigation as a short-term runbook.

lia: For the record, small dump of the short profile after mitigation:```
p99 before=860ms after=378ms
avg kernel_switches/node/min=12 -> 2
kvcache_evictions/min=48 -> 6
batcher.avg_microbatch_size=1.6 -> 3.2
```

sanjay: Great context. We'll let the debug run and then decide whether to make the admission tweak permanent or implement smarter tenant-aware coalescing. :thinking:
